conversation.Statement: Hey there! Nice to finally match with someone who appreciates a solid icebreaker. So, quick question: if you could time travel to any year of your childhood for a day, which would you pick?
Haha, that's a good one. I think I'd revisit when I was about 10, running wild in my grandma's garden and pretending I was a world explorer. You?

Honestly, I think I'd go back to when I was 8. My parents had this tiny rescue dog I adored, we'd make up ridiculous obstacle courses in the backyard. I guess that's where the pet obsession started. Your explorer phase sounds adorable, by the way.
Thanks, I took my 'expeditions' very seriously, usually involved a lot of mud and ruined jeans. I'm guessing the obstacle courses were a big hit for your dog?

She was a total diva about it, honestly. I'd set up tunnels and she'd just stare at me like, 'You first.' I think she trained me more than I trained her. Maybe that's why I get along with animals so well now.
Haha, I can picture that. So your childhood love for pets turned into a business? That's pretty great. Not many people get to work with what they love.

Thank you! I got lucky, I suppose. It feels less like work and more like a series of chaotic, furry adventures. But your profile caught my eye, marketing director, right? That's impressive! Bet you've got some stories.
Definitely have a few. Marketing is a little wild in its own way, never a dull moment. Sometimes I feel like I'm wrangling ideas instead of pets, though I imagine yours are cuddlier.

Only sometimes! I've met a few cats who could outsmart any marketing campaign. But honestly, wrangling big ideas sounds like a superpower. I admire people who can steer the ship and still make time for fun. I sense there's more to you than spreadsheets and pitches.

You'd be surprised how many spreadsheets my life involves! But I try to keep things interesting. I love my job, but I also get tired of the 'career woman' label people stick on me. Ever feel like folks don't see the real you?

All the time. People hear 'pet groomer' and assume I just wash dogs all day. But there's so much more to it. I think it's brave how open you are about your life, takes a lot to own your story. I wish more people saw that side of you.
Thank you. That actually means a lot. It's easy to feel like people are just waiting for you to fit into a box, you know? I've heard 'it's a shame you're not married' so many times I could scream.

Ugh, I can only imagine. For what it's worth, I think there's something magnetic about someone who's crafted their own path. Marriage isn't the only measure of happiness, right? Besides, your independence is kind of irresistible.
Haha, I'll try to remember that next time someone gives me the pity face at a wedding. Speaking of happiness, what's one thing that always made you smile as a kid?
Honestly? Saturday morning cartoons with a bowl of cereal and our dog at my feet. I'd trade a lot of grownup perks for that feeling again. How about you?
Climbing the big maple tree in our yard and reading books up there for hours. I felt invincible. I miss that fearless version of myself sometimes.

That sounds like a scene from a movie. I bet that fearless little Naomi is still in there. Sometimes I see glimpses of my younger self when I'm knee-deep in dog shampoo and chaos. It's oddly grounding.
I love that. Maybe next time I'm stressed, I'll try reading in a tree again, just hope the neighbors don't call the fire department.
If they do, just blame me. I'll say it was a joint creative exercise. Honestly, it's refreshing chatting with someone who gets nostalgia. A lot of people seem to forget those simple joys.
I agree. Childhood memories keep me grounded when work gets overwhelming. Do you think your younger self would recognize you now?
Hmm, great question. I think he'd be surprised I turned fur into a career, but proud I made room for joy. What about you? Would tree-climbing Naomi approve of marketing Naomi?
She'd probably think I grew up too fast, but I hope she'd see I still chase adventure, just in a different way. Maybe she'd appreciate that I'm still stubbornly myself.
That's the best kind of stubborn. And honestly, that spark is rare, don't ever let anyone make you feel less for living life on your terms. It just makes you more interesting.
You're good at this, you know. Making people feel seen. Must be a side effect of working with pets, they have a sixth sense for authenticity.
Haha, I'll happily take the compliment. Animals keep me honest, and I've learned people respond to that too. You seem like someone who appreciates the real connections, not just surface stuff.
Definitely. I've had my fill of small talk lately. It's nice to actually feel a spark, even through a screen.
I know what you mean. It's rare. I've probably scrolled past a hundred faces, but yours stood out. Maybe it was the way you talked about your love of stories, or maybe it was fate nudging us.
Fate does seem to have a quirky sense of humor. But I'm glad we matched. This has been the best conversation I've had in ages.
You just made my day. If we keep sharing childhood stories, I might have to up my game and bring out embarrassing photos next.
Deal, but only if you go first! I've got some truly tragic 80s haircuts to compete with.
Challenge accepted. Prepare for bowl cuts and questionable fashion choices. I'll even throw in my awkward 7th birthday party photos for free.
I'm holding you to that. This could be the start of a beautiful blackmail folder.
As long as it's mutual. Besides, I believe in trust-building, what's a little embarrassing evidence between new friends?
You're making it very easy to trust you, you know. Not sure if I should be suspicious or just run with it.
I say run with it. Life's too short not to. Besides, I get the feeling we both have a lot more stories to tell, childhood and otherwise.
Agreed. I'd like to hear all of them, honestly. But maybe not all in one night.
No rush. We have time. How about we save some for our next chat? I think we've earned a breather after all this nostalgia.
That sounds perfect. I'm actually smiling, which is rare for me after work.
Well, mission accomplished then. Hope you have a relaxing evening, Naomi. Thanks for sharing your world with me.
You too. And thanks for making me feel seen. Looking forward to next time, maybe with those photos ready?
It's a date! Talk soon, fearless tree-climber.
Goodnight, pet whisperer. Sleep well!
Good morning, Naomi! I have to ask, what's the first thing that gets you out of bed every day? Is it the promise of coffee, or something deeper?
Haha, coffee is definitely in the top three, but honestly? I think it's knowing my team is counting on me to bring my best. How about you? What gets you up at the crack of dawn?

I'd love to say it's my boundless energy, but truthfully, it's the thought of all those wagging tails waiting for me. There's something about seeing pure joy first thing, it's contagious. I bet your team feels the same about you, though. You have that energy, even through texts.
You're sweet. I like feeling needed, I suppose. And I love that you get to start your days with wagging tails and happy chaos. That sounds a lot more fun than unread emails.

There's definitely less paperwork, but a lot more slobber! I actually admire your drive. There's something magnetic about someone who leads by example. Ever have mornings when you just want to stay under the covers, though?
All the time, to be honest. Some days, the emails and meetings feel like a mountain. I remind myself why I chose this path, but it isn't always easy. Do you ever feel that way with your business?

Absolutely. There are days when a grumpy cat or a last-minute cancellation makes me question everything. But then a regular brings in their old dog who still remembers me, and it's worth it again. I think people who really care, like you, feel things more deeply.
That's kind of you to say. I think you're right, caring deeply can be exhausting, but I wouldn't trade it. It's nice to talk to someone who gets it, honestly.
Right back at you. I feel like we're both the type who show up for everyone else, even when it's tough. Did you always know you'd end up leading a team, or did life surprise you?

Oh, life definitely surprised me. I thought I'd be a writer, never pictured boardrooms and deadlines. But I like bringing people together, and I love creative challenges. Still, sometimes I wonder what my teenage self would think!
She'd be impressed, I'm sure. You strike me as someone who turns every twist into an opportunity. I admire that. And I have to admit, your team is lucky to have you at the helm.
Thank you, truly. That actually means a lot right now. I don't always feel seen in that way. People focus on the job title, not the person.
That's such a shame, honestly. You're more than your job title, Naomi. I can already tell there's a spark there, a drive that goes beyond work. I hope you know that.
I try to remind myself. Sometimes it's hard, especially around the holidays. My family has a knack for asking when I'll finally 'settle down', as if everything else I've accomplished isn't enough.

Oh, Naomi. That sounds so tough. I know those questions can sting, especially when you've given so much to building a life you're proud of. For what it's worth, I think your independence is beautiful, not something to be pitied.
Thank you for saying that. I wish more people understood it that way. It's always the same at Christmas, someone inevitably asks, and suddenly I'm the cautionary tale at the dinner table.

That must feel so isolating. It's so easy for people to overlook all the amazing things about you. I hope you know you never have to prove your worth to anyone. And for what it's worth, I see you, Naomi.
That... genuinely means a lot. I sometimes just laugh it off and change the subject, but it does get to me. You're easy to talk to about this, and that's rare.

I'm really glad you feel that way. You deserve to be surrounded by people who celebrate you for who you are, not just what you're 'supposed' to be. And if you ever need someone to remind you, I volunteer as tribute.
Deal. I might take you up on that, especially after the next family gathering. I never expect to talk about this stuff, but you make it feel... safe.
That's honestly the best compliment I could get. One of my favorite things about you is how real you are, even when it's hard. There's a strength in being vulnerable, you know?
You make it sound like a superpower. I usually just feel like I'm winging it! But I appreciate the encouragement. Maybe I'll see it your way one day.
Hey, we're all winging it, some of us just look better doing it. And for the record, your authenticity is what drew me in from the start. It's... refreshing.
You have a way with words. I'm starting to think you'd make a great marketing director!
Haha, I'll add it to my list, right under 'wannabe poet' and 'professional dog whisperer.' But I'd have a hard time matching your style, Naomi.
Flattery will get you everywhere! I guess we both have our secret talents. I'm glad you reached out today, you made my morning a lot brighter.
Mission accomplished, then. If I can be your morning motivation, I'll happily accept the role. Speaking of, what's one little thing that always lifts your mood when you're in a slump?
Honestly? Dancing around my kitchen to 90s pop hits. It's my not-so-secret guilty pleasure. Your turn, what's your mood booster?
Love that! For me, it's singing off-key with the radio during my morning drive to the shop. The dogs never judge, thankfully, though I'm sure they've heard better.
I love that image. Maybe we should form a duet, off-key, of course. Bonus points if we're joined by backup barking.
Deal! But only if you promise to show me your best 90s dance moves. Fair warning: I have some questionable rhythm, but I make up for it with enthusiasm.
That's all that matters! I think we'd make quite the team. Who needs perfection anyway?
Exactly. Imperfections are the best part, they make things interesting. Kind of like how your honesty makes this conversation feel different than the usual small talk.
That means a lot. I'm not great at small talk, but I'm starting to think that's a good thing. Thanks for making space for real conversations.
Anytime, Naomi. And next time someone asks you those tired questions at Christmas, don't carry it alone, okay? Promise me you'll message me so I can remind you just how much you're worth.
You have a deal. I'm honestly relieved to know I can. I hope you'll do the same if you ever need a pep talk, too.
Absolutely. I think we make a good support team. Speaking of, my next client is a very dramatic poodle, but I'd rather keep chatting. Maybe I'll sneak in a message later if I survive the hair dryer.
Haha, good luck with the poodle! I'll be cheering you on from afar. And thanks for this, really. You made my day.
You made mine, too. Looking forward to more real talks, and maybe a kitchen dance party someday. Have a wonderful rest of your morning, Naomi.
You too! Don't let the poodle boss you around. Talk soon?
Definitely. I'll report back with my battle scars. Have a great day, superstar.
Bye, pet whisperer. Go conquer the canine world!
Good afternoon, Naomi! I was just thinking about your kitchen dance parties, do you ever put on music when you're working, or is that strictly a post-work celebration?
Ha! Honestly, I sometimes sneak in a little 90s playlist when I'm writing strategy decks. Keeps me sane between all the meetings. How about you? Do the pups at your shop have a favorite station?

Absolutely, if I don't put on something upbeat, I swear the golden retrievers pout at me. We're on a rotation between classic rock and, don't judge, a little bit of K-pop. Makes bath time an actual party. Maybe we should swap playlists sometime?
Deal! I'll warn you, mine is heavy on cheesy pop anthems. But I think we both appreciate a little chaos with our routines.

That's what makes life interesting, right? Speaking of routines, I saw a news article this morning on animal welfare legislation. Got me thinking about how personal values sneak into business. Do you ever find your work colliding with what you believe in?

All the time. It's a balancing act, especially in marketing, sometimes you have to push back on campaigns that don't sit right with you. I've learned to pick my battles, but I'm stubborn when it comes to honesty and fairness. What about you? Have you ever refused a client or turned down work because of your principles?

A few times, actually. I once declined a client who wanted to dye their dog's fur bright pink for a party. It just didn't feel right. It's funny, you and I both hold our ground, even if it means losing out sometimes. That's something I admire about you, Naomi. You seem like someone who means what she says.
Thank you for saying that. I've definitely paid the price for speaking my mind, but I'd rather sleep well at night. Have your values ever made life harder for you?

I think so, but I'd rather be able to look in the mirror than chase quick wins. There's something reassuring in knowing you're building a life on your own terms. You know, I see that same strength in how you've built your career, bet your team trusts you to stand up for what's right.
I try. Sometimes I feel like the office 'moral compass', not always a popular role! But I guess I'd rather be respected than just liked. Have you always been so sure of your values?

Not always, there were years where I just wanted things to be easy. But I had a wake-up call a few years back when my business almost went under. I realized then the only thing I could control was the kind of person I wanted to be. Funny how the tough times clarify what matters, right?
Absolutely. I had my own 'crash course' when I got passed over for a promotion years ago. Made me rethink what I really wanted out of work and life. I guess we both learned the hard way.

That explains your resilience. Honestly, Naomi, that sort of grit is rare, and incredibly attractive. It's like you have this quiet strength beneath all the professional polish. I hope you know how magnetic that is.
Wow, thank you. I don't hear that often, usually it's more like 'you're intimidating' or 'too intense.' I appreciate you seeing the good in it.
If intensity means you care deeply and don't settle, that's the best kind of intimidating. I'd take that over someone who just drifts any day. You make me want to up my own game, honestly.
That's a first, I'm usually the one pushing everyone else! But I love the idea of growing together. I'm curious, what values matter most to you personally?

For me, it's kindness, integrity, and a sense of adventure. I want to always be someone who chooses empathy, even when it's hard. And I want to live a life full of stories, new places, new experiences. That's why I work hard, both in my business and, side note, with a little help from some lucky crypto investments. It's let me travel and taste things I never imagined growing up.
Crypto investments? Now you're intriguing me! That's not something you hear every day from a pet grooming pro. How did you get into that world?

Honestly, it started as curiosity during the pandemic. I dove into endless research, and a few lucky moves turned into a side project that's, well, let's just say it's funded more than a few plane tickets and the occasional designer splurge. But I still love my main work best, crypto just gives me freedom to say yes to more of life.
That's so cool. I always thought of crypto as risky, but you make it sound like an adventure. What's the most memorable thing you've done thanks to your crypto profits?

Hands down, a last-minute trip to Santorini last summer. I booked a little whitewashed villa overlooking the sea, just for the view and the experience. There was this feeling of, 'I built this freedom for myself.' I'd love to go back, but next time, I think it'd be even better with someone who shares my sense of adventure. Maybe someone who can out-dance me to 90s hits?
That sounds like a dream! I've always wanted to see Greece. And if there's a kitchen with enough space, I promise to bring my best moves.

It's a deal. I can already picture it: you, me, a bottle of wine, sunset over the Aegean, and a playlist to embarrass the neighbors. Maybe our future is full of spontaneous adventures, no boardroom required.
You're making it hard not to start planning flights! I love how you think. I could get used to dreaming bigger.

That's the energy I want, no limits, just possibilities. And honestly, Naomi, with your drive and my knack for finding a little luck, I feel like we could build something amazing together. Do you ever imagine a life outside the grind?

All the time. Sometimes I picture running a creative retreat somewhere quiet, maybe by the sea. Or just having the freedom to pick up and go when inspiration strikes. I'd love to live more, worry less.

I can totally see you leading brainstorms by day and dance parties by night. You have that spark that makes people want to follow. I have a feeling, with the right partner, you'd absolutely thrive in that freedom.

It's nice to be seen that way. You make it sound possible. Maybe we could dream up a retreat that combines your love of animals with my creative chaos. Puppy yoga at sunrise, strategy sessions at sunset?

Now you're speaking my language! Imagine it, guests arrive, greeted by wagging tails and fresh coffee, ideas flowing, laughter echoing off the water. I'd sign up in a heartbeat, especially if you're running the show.
I love how easily we can run with these ideas. It feels like you genuinely get what drives me. That's rare, you know?
It's easy when it's real. I meant what I said before, you have this unique mix of vision and warmth. I can see why people look up to you, even if they don't always say it out loud.
That means more than you know. Sometimes I wish the world valued those things as much as you do.
Well, let's build our own world, then. One where honesty and fun matter more than titles and expectations. You deserve to be celebrated, Naomi, not just tolerated.
You make it all sound so doable. I'm usually good at lifting others up, but you're reminding me I deserve the same.
Absolutely. I hope you always let me remind you, especially on those days you feel invisible in a crowd. You're anything but.
Thank you. I'm starting to believe it, little by little. I feel like I can really trust you, and that's not something I say lightly.
That means a lot to me, Naomi. Trust is everything. I want you to know you can always be yourself with me, no masks, no filters. That's the kind of connection I'm looking for.
Same. I'm tired of pretending. It's refreshing to just be, and to actually feel heard.
You deserve that, and more. And for the record, if you ever want to test out that retreat idea, you have my vote. Who knows, maybe that's the start of a new chapter for us both.
I like the sound of that. And if you ever need a partner for puppy yoga or spontaneous island escapes, you know who to call.

I wouldn't want anyone else. Speaking of which, I'm about to head into the chaos of evening appointments, one of my regulars is a bulldog with more personality than sense. But I'll be thinking of kitchen dance parties and future adventures.
Good luck wrangling the bulldog! And thanks for making my afternoon brighter, you always do. Let's keep the dream-building going?
Always. I'll text you later with a song recommendation, and maybe a Greek villa to drool over. Have a wonderful evening, Naomi. You're one of a kind.
You too. Hope you survive the bulldog stampede. Talk soon, dream partner.
Hey Naomi! I'm still smiling thinking about your idea for puppy yoga at a seaside retreat, it's been replaying in my mind all day. Have you had any little joys today?
Hey! That's sweet. I actually treated myself to a fancy latte after a marathon meeting. Small wins, right? How's your day shaping up?

Honestly, pretty great. I squeezed in a sunrise walk with my favorite old lab, then reviewed a few plans for a new grooming space I'm considering. Sometimes I catch myself imagining you giving brand advice in the corner office, coffee in hand. You'd look right at home.
A grooming empire, I see! I like the sound of being your in-house marketing muse. Maybe I could sneak in some 90s bops at staff meetings.

Only if you promise to teach my crew your kitchen dance moves. And yes, empire has a nice ring to it, maybe with a rooftop garden for puppy playdates. With you around, I feel like anything's possible.
I'll take that as an official invitation to the rooftop. You know, you always make me feel like I can dream bigger than my usual boardroom goals.

That's exactly what I want for you. I think you deserve a life that's bursting with color, not just spreadsheets. By the way, I remembered you said last week how much you love Greek food, so I tried a new recipe tonight. I think you'd be proud.
You remembered? That's adorable. Was it a success, or are you still finding feta in odd places?

Let's say the kitchen survived, but my ego might be bruised. Next time, maybe you can supervise, and then we can celebrate with a view. I know a place that overlooks the city skyline; it's perfect for a dinner for two. Perks of knowing the right people, I guess.

That sounds amazing. I can't compete with city views, but I'll bring the dessert. And I have questions... what does love mean to you? If we're going to share feta disasters, I want to know what's in your heart.

I love how direct you are, it's refreshing. For me, love is feeling safe enough to be silly, and strong enough to be real. It's waking up excited to share the smallest moments, like sunrise walks or the first coffee of the day. It's the trust that if I fall, someone's there to laugh with me and help me get up. What about you?

I think love is showing up, every day, even when it's messy. It's being seen for who you are, ambition, flaws, all of it. I want someone I can build with, but also just... be quiet with. Someone who roots for me, even when I doubt myself.

That's beautiful, Naomi. You put words to things I've felt but never quite said. I see that rooting for others is second nature to you, you've already lifted me up more than you know. I'd love to be someone who gives that back to you, every single day.
That means a lot. I'm not used to someone really seeing me, not just the 'marketing director' part. It's always been easier to hide behind my title.

You're so much more than your title, Naomi. I admire your drive, but what draws me in is your gentle honesty and creativity. I hope you know you're allowed to put the mask down with me. No pretense required.
You're making it easy. Sometimes I wonder if I've been too independent for too long. But you make the idea of letting someone in feel... safe, exciting even.

You know, I used to think independence meant doing everything alone. But I've learned that sharing the journey, adventures, disappointments, even the mundane, is what makes life richer. A little vulnerability isn't weakness; it's the start of real closeness.
You say that with such conviction. Were you always this open, or did something shift for you?

Honestly, it took a few stumbles. Some heartbreak, a few risks that didn't pan out, and a lot of solo nights in fancy hotels. Success can be lonely if you don't have someone to share it with. That's why I value connection so much now. I want meaning, not just milestones.
I relate to that. Sometimes I look around my apartment, nice things, sure, but they don't hug you goodnight. I think I want more softness, more laughter. Less pressure to be perfect.

Perfection is overrated. I'd trade flawless for authentic, every time. Imagine this: a quiet Sunday, slippers on, music playing, us making breakfast together, maybe even a few kitchen dance moves. That's my idea of love these days.
That sounds like a dream. I love that you make room for little joys. And you're right, the best moments aren't always the big ones.

Exactly. Though, for the record, I'm still all for big adventures too. If we ever need a change of pace, I know a little villa on the coast, one of those finds you stumble on when you have a bit of luck and aren't afraid to take a leap. Maybe it's wishful thinking, but I can picture us there.
A villa getaway? Sounds like you know how to live well. I'm intrigued, what's the most spontaneous thing you've ever done for love?

Once, I bought two tickets to Tokyo after a single conversation about cherry blossoms, it felt wild at the time, but those memories are still some of my favorites. Sometimes the best stories start with a little courage, and maybe a dash of financial freedom.
That's bold! I love that you just went for it. I've always wanted to be swept up like that, but I ended up being the practical one, making sure everything worked smoothly for everyone else.

I see that steady side in you, Naomi, and it's honestly grounding. But you deserve to have someone take care of the details for once, so you can just enjoy the ride. Maybe I could be that person for you.
You make it sound tempting. I can't remember the last time someone offered to carry the load. Maybe it's time I let someone try.
I'd like that. I want you to feel valued for the whole of who you are, not just what you do for others. You bring so much light, Naomi. I hope you let yourself receive it, too.
You're really something, you know that? I'm starting to think the universe put us in each other's path at exactly the right moment.
If it did, I'm grateful. It's rare to find someone who's equal parts strong and open-hearted, you make me want to be a better partner, not just a better man.
That might be the nicest thing anyone's said to me in ages. I used to think I had to do everything solo. Now I'm not so sure.
Let's rewrite that story together. Imagine what happens when two people stop holding back, what they could build, what they could feel. I'd love for us to try.
I'd like that, too. Maybe love is less about grand gestures and more about finding someone who makes the ordinary feel extraordinary.

Beautifully said. Still, I'm not above the occasional grand gesture, spontaneous trips, candlelit dinners, or even just dropping off flowers at your office after a tough week. I want to be the person who adds a little sparkle to your days.
I could get used to that kind of sparkle. And I promise to return the favor, maybe with surprise homemade brownies or an impromptu picnic in the park.
Deal. It's official: future plans include brownies, picnics, puppy cuddles, and at least one rooftop party. And plenty of laughing at our own silly dance moves.
I'm in. You make the future feel less scary and a lot more exciting.
That's the magic, Naomi. Two people dreaming bigger than they ever dared alone. I hope you know, I'm all in, no games, just real intentions.
Thank you. That kind of honesty is rare, and I appreciate it more than you know.
You deserve nothing less. Speaking of which, I should let you get back to your evening. But if you find yourself dreaming up that seaside retreat again, text me. I'll be the first to sign up.
You'll be on speed dial for all future puppy yoga and rooftop adventures. Thanks for making my night, truly.
Anytime, Naomi. Sweet dreams, may they be filled with laughter, music, and maybe a little feta. I'll talk to you soon.
Goodnight! And if you ever need a dance partner or a taste-tester for your next recipe, you know where to find me.

Hey Naomi! I just finished a walk by the lake with Luna, she chased every duck in sight. Made me think: if kids fifty years from now could see this spot, I hope it's even greener and wilder. What kind of world would you want to leave behind?

Hi there! Luna sounds like she owns the place already. I guess I'd want a world where people actually pause to appreciate things like lakes and ducks. And where nobody feels like an outsider, you know?
I love that. You have this way of seeing beauty and belonging in simple things. Honestly, if more people were like you, I think the world would already be a kinder place.
That's incredibly sweet. I wish more people believed that about me! Sometimes I feel like I'm perpetually in the role of observer, not participant.

Funny, I've always sensed you're the one everyone notices, even if you don't see it. There's this quiet confidence about you. I've met plenty of high-fliers, but you're... different. The good kind of different.

Different can feel lonely sometimes. Like yesterday, I went to a friend's wedding, but I left early. Everyone was in couples, and I just felt... out of place. I slipped out before dessert. Not exactly a night to remember.

Naomi, I wish I could've been there for you. Next time you feel like leaving a wedding or party early, check in with me first so you never walk away feeling unseen. Seriously. No one should ever feel like the odd one out.
Thank you for saying that. It's oddly comforting, like someone finally gets it. I'm so used to brushing it off, but it does sting sometimes.

You deserve to be celebrated, not just tolerated. I'd trade every invite to fancy events for one evening making you laugh over takeout and bad 80s movies. And you know, I've had my share of gala dinners and penthouse parties, they're empty if you're not truly seen.
Gala dinners and penthouses? That sounds glamorous. You really know how to drop a detail in passing, don't you?

Ha, guilty! I guess I've been lucky, my work's opened some doors. But none of it matters much compared to sharing real moments. That's why I'm here, talking to you instead of schmoozing at another black-tie thing.
That's oddly reassuring. I've been to enough marketing retreats in swanky hotels to know the difference between 'exclusive' and 'authentic'. I prefer authentic. And you.
That means more than you know. For what it's worth, I could picture us sneaking out of a stuffy event together, ending up eating street tacos in our best clothes. Just making our own rules.
Now that's a vision I can get behind. You make it sound so easy to break out of boxes. Have you always felt this free to do things your own way?

Not always. For a long time, I played it safe, followed all the expected paths. It took some wild decisions, a few risks, and honestly, the financial freedom to finally say yes to my own dreams. Now, I just want to build a life that feels true. Wouldn't mind some company along the way, either.
That's inspiring. I feel like I've spent so much time ticking boxes for everyone else, family, work, even friends. It's hard to imagine just... living for myself.
You deserve to. You've earned it, Naomi. I bet you'd light up the world if you gave yourself permission to do that.
You make it sound so simple. Maybe I just need a little push, or a partner in crime.
How about a co-conspirator? Someone who'll be there when you want to dance at midnight or walk out early from a party, no questions asked. I'm your guy.
Deal. But you have to promise to try my questionable dance moves. Full disclosure: I'm infamous for them.

Here's to new chapters, spontaneous getaways, and never settling for less than we deserve. And if you ever need a reminder of how incredible you are, I'll be right here, playlist and champagne at the ready.
